subject: Career
title: Information as Currency
description: A 60-second lesson on Information as Currency.

hook.text: She knew about the reorg three weeks before the announcement. That knowledge was worth more than her title.

buildup.text: In organizations, information is power. Who knows what — and when — determines who influences decisions.

discovery.text: People who sit at information crossroads — between teams, departments, or levels — become indispensable.

twist.text: Hoarding information creates short-term power but long-term distrust. Strategic sharing builds both.

climax.text: Be a conduit, not a bottleneck. Share information generously and people will share back.

punchline.text: Information hoarded loses value. Information shared builds power.

quiz.question: Why is information considered currency in office politics?
options: Who knows what and when determines who influences decisions

details.summary: In organizations, information is a form of power. People who control access to key data, decisions, or context wield influence disproportionate to their formal authority. Information sharing and withholding are both political acts.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing information as currency explains why some colleagues hoard knowledge and others share it strategically. Understanding this dynamic helps you position yourself as knowledgeable.
takeaways: Being a reliable source of information builds trust and influence
Information hoarding is often a defensive political strategy
Sharing information generously builds reciprocity and social capital

faq.question: How do you deal with colleagues who hoard information to maintain power?
faq.answer: Build alternative information channels through cross-functional relationships and direct communication with leadership. When information hoarders realize their monopoly is broken, they often shift to sharing because hoarding no longer provides an advantage.

faq.question: Is strategic information sharing the same as gossip or leaking?
faq.answer: No. Strategic sharing involves providing relevant, appropriate information to the right people for constructive purposes. Gossip and leaking involve sharing confidential or harmful information for personal advantage or entertainment, which damages trust.
